paid_market_gaps.gap: Leading MCP governance vendors (Runlayer, MintMCP) publish no prices and offer no self-serve; small teams cannot evaluate or buy
Free Docker MCP Gateway has one shared token; per-user access, per-tool policy and audit require a separate enterprise contract
Azure APIM v2 tiers lack tool-level MCP control; dynamic tool lists cannot be governed by Agent 365
External audit connectors and fine-grained authorization need Descope Growth ($799/mo); lower tiers keep audit 1 week-1 month

wtp_evidence: Public paid tiers (TrueFoundry $25/user/mo, Descope $249-$799/mo) and Runlayer raising a $30M Series A (total funding $42M) for enterprise MCP governance show buyers pay; post-purchase complaints not found.
bundling_note: AWS AgentCore includes Identity at no extra charge via Gateway (Policy billed per authorization), Cloudflare MCP portals are available to all customers, and Docker's gateway is free MIT.
summary: Crowded and fast-bundling: funded gateways (Runlayer, MintMCP), identity incumbents (Auth0, Descope) and clouds (AWS, Cloudflare, Microsoft) all cover it. Only a narrow wedge remains, e.g. self-serve per-agent credentials and audit for mid-market teams across clouds.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Version-banner ASV findings flag backported-patched Apache/PHP/OpenSSH; merchants must manually dispute false positives each scan

wtp_evidence: Merchants pay small amounts: ASV scans $81.90/year (Sectigo HackerGuardian via reseller) to $185/year (Clone Systems, 1 target), processor PCI fees ~$120/year, non-compliance fees ~$20-$30+/month push validation; buyers treat it as a junk-fee chore, and hosted payment pages shrink scope.
bundling_note: Processors bundle scans/SAQs, hosted checkouts (Stripe) cut server scope, hosts sell add-ons, Wazuh gives free PCI FIM, and AWS Security Hub/Defender Plan 2 include PCI checks/FIM.
summary: Crowded, commoditized market of cheap ASV scans and FIM, bundled by processors, hosts and clouds. Thin opening: automated backport-aware false-positive dispute and remediation for hosts/MSPs serving self-hosted PHP merchants; low ACV.

summary: Weak opening: build-time SBOM generation and signing is commoditized and bundled by GitHub, Docker, GitLab and AWS. Only niche wedge: embedded C/C++ firmware vendors needing CRA/BSI TR-03183-conformant build SBOMs.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Enterprise platforms sell via large annual commits (Pillar $175k, Lasso $20k+); small teams have few paid options besides Knostic.
Native agent permission rules are pattern-based; argument rules are bypassable by compound commands, pushing users to sandboxing.
Headless/non-interactive agent runs often auto-approve all tool calls, with no read-only or plan mode.
Per-call policy engines do not yet correlate sequences of individually allowed calls into malicious workflows.

wtp_evidence: Public prices exist: Pillar platform $175,000/12 months and Lasso for GenAI Chatbots $20,000 annual commit (12 months) on AWS Marketplace, Knostic Kirin $15/user/month.
bundling_note: Agent vendors ship free permission rules and managed deny settings (Claude Code), AWS meters Cedar tool-call policy in AgentCore, and Microsoft and Docker give away open-source MCP policy gateways.
summary: Crowded and consolidating (SentinelOne-Prompt, well-funded Pillar, Lasso, Runlayer) with free native and cloud controls. Narrow opening: cheap cross-agent policy enforcement for small and mid-size dev teams, including headless/CI agent runs, below enterprise annual commits.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Enterprise decisioning tools (RadarFirst, BreachRx, OneTrust) quote-only; no self-serve product for small NIS2 or FTC-covered firms
Enterprise GRC offers NIS2 three-stage BSI reporting only as add-on or configuration, not ready workflow
Multi-regime triage (NIS2, DORA, Reg S-P, FTC) at one incident: hundreds of concurrent obligations overwhelm processes
No tool drafts filings straight into national portals; BSI portal submissions are manual via ELSTER-based accounts

wtp_evidence: Enterprises buy quote-only tools (BreachRx: 100+ customers incl. Amex, Coinbase; $15M Series A in May 2025); SMB NIS2 platforms start ~EUR 10,000.
bundling_note: Cloud providers don't give away jurisdictional notification logic, but GRC/privacy suites (OneTrust, ServiceNow, NIS2 compliance platforms) and MDR/incident-response retainers bundle reporting, and authorities run free portals.
summary: Established enterprise tools and notification services exist; the opening is a self-serve, low-cost multi-regime reporting clock for SMB and mid-market firms (NIS2 'important entities', FTC-covered non-banks, small RIAs/broker-dealers), likely sold via MSSPs/MDR.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Small municipalities (Hodonín, est. CZK 1.5M) tender full PAM delivery and had to re-issue the tender
Tenders scored 100% on lowest price favour bundled integrator bids; no product differentiation is rewarded
Lithuanian-only tender documents and 60-month service scope need local integrator partners, not direct vendor sales
Czech NIS2 lower-regime decree brings many small entities under access-control duties with limited budgets

wtp_evidence: Public buyers budget real money for PAM: a regional hospital estimates CZK 13.2M over 60 months, a town CZK 1.5M; but awards go on lowest price, squeezing margins.
bundling_note: Entra ID P2 includes select PIM for cloud roles, but on-prem session recording, vaulting and rotation that these tenders specify remain paid products.
summary: Procurement is real but crowded and integrator-led, judged on lowest price. A startup could only win as a cheap, quickly deployable, EU-sovereign PAM sold through local integrators to small NIS2-regulated public bodies; thin margins.

paid_market_gaps.gap: GitLab shows only one shortest path, only for vulnerable dependencies and a limited set of package managers
GitHub's transitive path labels cover only npm and Maven and need dependency-graph submission enabled
Dependency-Track users lack the parent/root dependency of a vulnerable component in finding views
Linking SBOM components to deployed applications and containers for impact analysis stays largely manual

wtp_evidence: Buyers pay for SCA suites that include dependency paths and impact search (Semgrep Team $30/contributor/month, GitHub Code Security $30/committer/month, JFrog Enterprise X from $950/month with Advanced Security as a paid add-on bundle), but the capability is sold as a feature, not standalone.
bundling_note: GitHub Dependabot alerts show transitive paths at no extra cost and GitLab Ultimate, JFrog and Semgrep include dependency paths and impact search in existing SCA plans.
summary: No standalone opening: dependency paths and impact search are standard SCA features, bundled by GitHub and GitLab. Narrow wedge: reverse-impact across heterogeneous third-party/container SBOMs for Dependency-Track users, likely an add-on, not a company.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Czech public bodies want EDR/XDR, SIEM and 60-month MDR as one turnkey contract meeting Act 264/2025
Buyers struggle to get bids: Plzen hospital tender republished repeatedly with extended deadlines
On-premises XDR with supplied hardware required alongside SIEM and DLP, misfitting cloud-only vendors
Leading EDR vendors sell SIEM and MDR as separately quoted add-ons, not integrated priced bundles

wtp_evidence: Plzen University Hospital budgets CZK 76 million excl. VAT for 68 months of EDR/XDR+SIEM+MDR; Prague SSHMP tenders SIEM/XDR/DLP; EDR lists at $60-$185 per device/year.
bundling_note: Microsoft ingests Defender XDR alerts into Sentinel free and bundles Defender in M365 E5; Elastic now includes endpoint protection in SIEM pricing.
summary: Crowded vendor market, but real paid demand: Czech public bodies pay millions for compliant integrated EDR+SIEM+MDR. Opening is for local integrators/MSSPs packaging existing products for Act 264/2025 tenders, not a new product.
